Dear Chris

I'm interested in unilateral structural connectivity between the subcortical structures. I use FSL PROBTRAKX with matrix option on DTI data. I wish to use the brainGraph supplying directly the fdt_network_matrices generated by FSL tractorgaphy.
Hence, I have created a custom hemispheric atlas data.table with the subcortical structures following the required format (see below). Is it correct? or I should follow the bi-hemispheric atlas model?

> print(custom_atlas.L_up)
name x.mni y.mni z.mni lobe hemi index name.full
1 dentN.L 52.1 33.3 18.5 Cerebllum L 1 dentate nucleus left
2 redN.L 47.0 53.2 31.9 SCGM L 2 red nucleus left
3 SN.L 49.5 54.9 29.9 SCGM L 3 substantia nigria left
4 PAG 44.6 47.9 31.8 SCGM L 4 periaqueductal gray
5 STN.L 50.0 56.5 33.0 SCGM L 5 subthalamic nucleus left
6 Gpe.L 54.8 61.5 35.8 SCGM L 6 globus pallidum left
7 put.L 57.5 63.2 36.2 SCGM L 7 putamen left
8 thal.L 50.0 53.6 39.4 SCGM L 8 thalamus left
>

Anyway, I'm getting an error (below) after running the 02_create_graphs.R (I've followed step-by step your codes in the brainGraph_UserGuide v.2.7.0, pages 38-45)

[1] "Threshold 1/10; group 1; 17:23:06"
Error in { : task 1 failed - "invalid first argument"

If I switch to, for example,
atlas <- "aal116"
the code runs without error at this step (of course the labels are wrong, but I just wanted to test). However, on the next step - 03_getting_graph_measures.R, nonetheless the group-level code runs smoothly and I can see the generated dt.V.group and dt.G.group, I continue to get error in the subject level:

> # SUBJECT-LEVEL
> #===============================================================================
> dt.V <- vector('list', length=length(groups))
> for (i in seq_along(groups)) {
+ dt.V[[i]] <- lapply(g[[i]], llply, vertex_attr_dt, groups[i])
+ dt.V[[i]] <- rbindlist(lapply(dt.V[[i]], rbindlist))
+ }
> dt.V <- rbindlist(dt.V)
> dt.G <- rbindlist(Map(function(x, y)
+ rbindlist(lapply(x, graph_attr_dt, y)),
+ g, as.list(groups)))

Error in g.list[[1]] : subscript out of bounds

Could you, please, help me with these two issues.

All my best
Gayane

Thanks. I am not *exactly* sure why you are getting an error, but try the following:

* The "atlas" variable should be a character string indicating the *name* of the atlas. In your case,
atlas <- 'custom_atlas.L'

* The atlas object itself must be a *data.table*, not a data.frame. So
setDT(custom_atlas.L)

* The "name" column in your atlas must be character, not factor. After the previous step, you can do
custom_atlas.L[, name := as.character(name)]

* The "Group" column (in "covars.dti") must exactly match the "groups" variable. Here, the "groups" variable has the "TAU" in all uppercase; in "covars.dti" they are all lowercase. It would be easier to change the "groups" variable:
groups <- covars.dti[, levels(Group)]

To ensure that the atlas and covariates are always data.table objects, you can use "fread" instead of "read.csv". In this case, you would probably have to specify that "lobe" and "hemi" should be factor variables.

Please try the above changes and see if it works.
Chris

* The "atlas" variable should be a character string indicating the *name* of the atlas. In your case,
atlas <- 'custom_atlas.L'

setDT(custom_atlas.L)

custom_atlas.L[, name := as.character(name)]

groups <- covars.dti[, levels(Group)]

Thanks. I am not *exactly* sure why you are getting an error, but try the following:

* The "atlas" variable should be a character string indicating the *name* of the atlas. In your case,

custom_atlas.L[, name := as.character(name)]

groups <- covars.dti[, levels(Group)]

Thanks. I am not *exactly* sure why you are getting an error, but try the following:

* The "atlas" variable should be a character string indicating the *name* of the atlas. In your case,
atlas <- 'custom_atlas.L'

* The atlas object itself must be a *data.table*, not a data.frame. So
setDT(custom_atlas.L)

* The "name" column in your atlas must be character, not factor. After the previous step, you can do
custom_atlas.L[, name := as.character(name)]

* The "Group" column (in "covars.dti") must exactly match the "groups" variable. Here, the "groups" variable has the "TAU" in all uppercase; in "covars.dti" they are all lowercase. It would be easier to change the "groups" variable:
groups <- covars.dti[, levels(Group)]

To ensure that the atlas and covariates are always data.table objects, you can use "fread" instead of "read.csv". In this case, you would probably have to specify that "lobe" and "hemi" should be factor variables.

Please try the above changes and see if it works.
Chris

* The "atlas" variable should be a character string indicating the *name* of the atlas. In your case,

custom_atlas.L[, name := as.character(name)]

groups <- covars.dti[, levels(Group)]

To ensure that the atlas and covariates are always data.table objects, you can use "fread" instead of "read.csv". In this case, you would probably have to specify that "lobe" and "hemi" should be factor variables.
